page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 16 physical cores of an ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance type, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 259.29 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reaches 113.31 GB/sec, both ranking in the strong category (top 25%). Single-threaded gzip compression at 32.27 GB/sec and Geekbench multi-core execution at 16780.0 also demonstrate strong performance. Other computing metrics, including stress-ng CPU tests, Redis SET operations at 33.77 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 41.54 GB/sec, fall within the average tier.

Lacking simultaneous multithreading, each of the 16 vCPUs operates on a dedicated physical core, ensuring consistent execution times without resource sharing. However, the absence of AVX and AMX instruction sets limits its utility for specialized x86 vector math or hardware-accelerated matrix operations. Given its high memory bandwidth and strong database operation scores, the c4a-standard-16 is suited for memory-bound applications, database operations, web serving, text processing, and general-purpose ARM64 development workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is an arm64 virtual machine powered by a 16-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs with no hyperthreading, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the c4a-standard-16 exhibits top-tier memory performance, highlighted by a Passmark memory score in the top 10% and strong uncached large-block memory bandwidth. While single-core stress-ng and web serving throughput align with average tiers, its multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput make it highly efficient for memory-sensitive workloads. The instance is suited for database operations, text processing, web serving, and general-purpose ARM-native applications.
